answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by completing tasks that counterparties later confirm, with each confirmed job tied to a scarce, nonrefundable bond. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting one operator across many accounts does not multiply influence; each account must independently build a record and lock capital. An atlas of task links can expose repeated counterparties, while umber and reef label separate service niches. The attacker pays in bonds, time, and real work, and risks forfeiture when claims are disputed.
